MEMBER.NAME: Prospanica
MEMBER.DESC: Prospanica has advocated for Hispanic business professionals for 30 years. Since our founding as the National Society of Hispanic MBAs in 1988, we’ve hosted annual career and professional development conferences, connecting thousands of Hispanics to graduate programs, subject matter experts, corporations, and each other.  Prospanica has given over $8 million in scholarships for graduate education, and many of those recipients have led our professional chapters and university chapters across the US and Puerto Rico, advancing diversity causes in their own communities. In 2016, as Hispanics continued to occupy a growing portion of the nation’s demographics, we rebranded as Prospanica to broaden our mission to serve all Hispanic professionals.

MEMBER.NAME: Tau Beta Pi
MEMBER.DESC:
Tau Beta Pi is the only engineering honor society representing the entire engineering profession. It is the nation's second-oldest honor society, founded at Lehigh University in 1885 to mark in a fitting manner those who have conferred honor upon their Alma Mater by distinguished scholarship and exemplary character as students in engineering, or by their attainments as alumni in the field of engineering, and to foster a spirit of liberal culture in engineering colleges.

There are now collegiate chapters at 247 US colleges and universities, 44 active alumni chapters in 16 districts across the country, and a total initiated membership of approximately 594,000.

MEMBER.NAME: The Institue for Operations Research and Management Science
MEMBER.DESC:
With over 12,500 members from around the globe, INFORMS is the leading international association for professionals in operations research and analytics.

INFORMS promotes best practices and advances in operations research, management science, and analytics to improve operational processes, decision-making, and outcomes through an array of highly-cited publications, conferences, competitions, networking communities, and professional development services.

MEMBER.NAME: The Institue of Industrial and Systems Engineers
MEMBER.DESC: Systems world view. Productivity. Efficiency. These are words that describe the distinctive attributes of industrial engineering, and IISE is the world's largest professional society dedicated solely to the support of the industrial engineering profession and individuals involved with improving quality and productivity.

MEMBER.NAME: The Society for Hispanic Professional Engineers
MEMBER.DESC:
The Society of Hispanic Professional Engineers (SHPE) was founded in Los Angeles, California, in 1974 by a group of engineers employed by the city of Los Angeles. Their objective was to form a national organization of professional engineers to serve as role models in the Hispanic community.

The concept of Networking was the key basis for the organization. SHPE quickly established two student chapters to begin the network that would grow to encompass the nation as well as reach countries outside the United States. Today, SHPE enjoys a strong but independent network of professional and student chapters throughout the nation.

MEMBER.NAME: The Society of Manufacturing Engineers
MEMBER.DESC:
Manufacturing has long been central to global economies and prosperity, creating value and opportunity for communities, workers and their families. It is absolutely vital.

And, SME has been supporting the manufacturing industry for over 85 years. Working closely with manufacturing professionals, companies, educators, schools and communities, we share knowledge and resources that generate solutions to manufacturing industry challenges.

MEMBER.NAME: The Society of Mexican-American Engineers and Scientists
MEMBER.DESC: MAES – Latinos in Science and Engineering (MAES) was founded in Los Angeles in 1974 by a group of professional engineers to advance and increase the number of Latinos in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics by creating opportunities and fostering recognition through its professional, technical, and outreach activities. The mission of MAES is to promote, cultivate, and honor excellence in education and leadership among Latino engineers and scientists. MAES is a 501(c)(3) non-profit corporation. For more information, visit http://mymaes.org.

CONGRANT.TITLE: Innovative Talented and Achieving Scholars (iTAS) Program: Low Income and Transfer Student Integration and Onboarding Pathways to Increase Student Academic and Career Success in the RGV Engineering & Computer Science Programs
CONGRANT.ABSTRACT: The ITAS S-STEM program’s mission is to build a foundation in the Rio Grande Valley community and meet the NSF S-STEM goal of supporting and enabling low-income, talented domestic students to pursue successful careers in promising STEM fields. This project will contribute to educate technicians, engineers, and scientists through scholarships and innovative evidence-based curricular and co-curricular activities for all eligible students in the College of Engineering at the University of Texas Rio Grande Valley (UTRGV). In this proposal, the team at UTRGV, the second largest Hispanic Serving institution in the nation, will also collaborate with South Texas College (STC), the largest community college in the south Texas region with a current S-STEM grant, to increase the success and retention of local transfers students identified to complete their BS degrees.

CONGRANT.TITLE: Better Border for a Better America University Transportation Center (B3A UTC)
CONTENT_GOAL: GOAL 16: Peace and Justice Strong Institutions
GOAL 17: Partnerships to achieve the Goal
GOAL 8: Decent Work and Economic Growth
CONGRANT.ABSTRACT:
The William and Barbara Leonard Transportation Center at California State University at San Bernardino (lead), in collaboration with the Texas A&M Transportation Institute of the Texas A&M University System, the Arizona State University, the New Mexico State University, the University of Texas Rio Grande Valley, the San Bernardino Valley College, and the Dona Ana Community College, is pleased to submit this proposal to create a Tier 1 University Transportation Center (UTC) addressing the statutory research priority of “improving mobility of people and goods.” The proposed Better Border for a Better America (B3A) UTC focuses on enhancing the efficient mobility of people and goods across the U.S.-Mexico border.
The unique contribution of the B3A UTC’s research agenda is that it addresses the mobility challenges of people and goods across the southern border - critical for the country’s economic prosperity - while addressing the challenges that growing trade imposes on U.S. border communities. This is a complex problem that has not been sufficiently addressed in transportation research. The complexity of improving the mobility of people and goods is compounded in an international border environment by border regulations, the international jurisdictions involved, and the social and cultural dimensions. It requires not only a multi- disciplinary approach, but also a deep understanding of the challenges and the border communities that are impacted, as well as the importance of trade to the U.S., Mexico, border states, and local economies.
The focus on improving mobility across the U.S.-Mexico border is particularly timely, given its national importance from an economic, national security, and justice perspective. In 2021, almost $1.5 billion in goods traded with Mexico crossed the U.S-Mexico border each day by truck or rail. Similarly, in 2021, 341,095 people crossed the border per day as pedestrians or in passenger vehicles. This growth is expected to continue with the signing of the 2020 U.S.-Mexico-Canada Agreement and the reconfiguration of global supply chains resulting in nearshoring and friend-shoring.
There are several research questions that arise in the context of investing in and modernizing border infrastructure to enhance the efficient cross-border mobility of travelers and goods. Growing trade presents serious challenges to U.S. border communities, which are among the poorest in the nation and have for years borne the brunt of the negative impacts of international trade (e.g., traffic congestion and pollution). The B3A UTC will focus on exploring infrastructure, operational, technology, and policy/regulatory initiatives to prepare the border for the demands of the future, while recognizing the justice/equity, economic, global competitiveness, workforce development, and environmental (including resiliency and sustainability) impacts.
In doing this, the B3A UTC will address several key challenges identified by U.S. DOT under the research priority areas, including freight logistics, data, and workforce; transportation equity; demand management; operations; environmental justice; resilience; and supply chain. The B3A UTC will also consider various candidate technologies identified by U.S. DOT in addressing these challenges, such as: vehicle-to-infrastructure, vehicle-to-pedestrian, vehicle-to-everything; simulation and modeling; artificial intelligence and machine learning; and community engagement. More specifically, the B3A UTC will explore the following focus areas:
Infrastructure capacity solutions, such as heavy weight corridors that serve the international crossings and reduce the need for Mexican carriers to unload trucks before crossing the U.S.-Mexico border;Modernization and new technologies to help increase throughput on existing infrastructure, such as biometric and x-ray machines that remove the need for interaction with customs officials, smart border technologies, and new and emerging technologies to future-proof U.S.-Mexico cross-border transportation infrastructure;Operational Improvements of crossing and transportation corridors serving crossings to enhance capacity usage, such as unified cargo inspections and dynamic message signs to route traffic to less congested crossings; and New policy/ regulatory paradigms to improve cross-border governance and operations in the 21st century, as well as to overcome barriers to efficient cross-border movement, such as addressing the requirement for trains to change crews at the U.S.-Mexico border.These focus areas will be explored through the lenses of:
justice/ equity - ensuring the research contributes to a more just outcome by promoting equity and equitable access for border communities to cross-border transportation services and to trade opportunities while mitigating impacts on disadvantaged and minority communities. economic impacts - ensuring the research considers the economic development/growth opportunities and impacts on border communities. climate, sustainability, and resiliency - ensuring the research contributes to a more resilient and sustainable U.S.-Mexico border transportation system, as well as mitigating the environmental impacts of increased cross-border travel and trade, such as increased criteria pollutants and greenhouse gas emissions. global competitiveness - ensuring the research addresses supply chain efficiencies, redundancies, and overall global competitiveness. workforce development - ensuring the research promotes training of border residents and access to higher paying jobs.
By exploring these four focus areas through these five lenses, the B3A UTC will contribute to improving cross-border mobility while addressing the potential impacts on border communities to ensure an equitable sharing of the benefits and opportunities associated with increased trade. This holistic approach addresses the U.S. DOT’s strategic objectives of economic strength and global competitiveness, equity, climate and sustainability, and transformation.

CONGRANT.TITLE: CAREER PROPOSAL: Analysis and Decision Support for National Security Sensitive Queueing Systems – A U.S. Commercial Border Crossing Tool
CONGRANT.ABSTRACT:
Project Summary
This integrated research and education project proposes a multi-tier solution to a stochastic, non-stationary, and terminating queuing system that is visible in the congestion of the commercial border crossing process at the United States (U.S.) border.  This proposal focuses on a multiple tier approach to improve this system by utilizing technical queueing theory aspects on truck lines, simulation modeling, and data analytics to influence human decision behavior, while integrating educational components to facilitate the dissemination of information to the multinational community and region, without affecting the security procedures or the costs at the Ports of Entry (POE).  Additional benefits that can be realized include congestion reduction on both sides of the border, improved utilization of major facilities and infrastructure, and reduced pollution generated by the idling of commercial trucks. According to the U.S. Department of Transportation (US DOT, 2016), over 11 million commercial trucks came into the U.S. in 2015, not including private vehicles and pedestrian traffic, through one of over 100 major border POEs.  At the Southern U.S. border over 5.5 million commercial trucks entered the country through the over 20 POEs (BTS, 2016).  However, securing our southwest border from terrorist interventions, undocumented immigrants, and the illegal flow of drugs and guns has dominated the ability to efficiently and effectively process people, goods and traffic. Increasing security and inspection requirements are seriously affecting transit times. Each POE is configured as a multi-commodity, prioritized queueing network which rarely, if ever, operates in steady-state. Therefore, the challenge is to balance 1) a reduction of wait time and its variance; 2) effectively utilize resources and minimize cost of POE operations, and 3) the sustainment of a security levels through Agent training, inspection and detection.
The intellectual merit of this proposal is based on using queueing theory and simulation on the border crossing process to implement methodologies that addresses port utilization and efficiency, which affects wait times, without increasing costs or affecting security procedures. An analytical model of a stochastic, non-stationary, and terminating queuing system is challenging because of the number of states in the system given the trucks at the POE.  A simulation model, validated through the analytical model, will serve to implement and test throughput improvement methodologies that do not affect cost or security procedures.  Improvements include the Dynamic Reallocation Methodology (DRM), lane availability policies, and the effect of influencing supply chain arrival data of commercial trucks. The second contribution addresses inspection (service) times under time-varying arrivals (demands). By developing secondary inspection policies, primary inspection time variance can be reduced. In the simulation model, a Markovian service time will be assumed first. However, prior work and field data suggest a general distribution that will be estimated using a Coxian k-phased approximation.  The third contribution is the development of a mobile app that will serve as a decision support application for the general public.  Current wait time sources are estimates at best.  An application that utilizes historical data can influence companies and people to select alternatives to congested border crossing points, and improve efficiencies.
The broader impact of this proposal applies to the international region that includes south Texas and northern Mexico.  Improvements will benefit border communities economically and the general population through increased security. Finally, by incorporating into current educational efforts, new engineers and the general public can be educated to make better decisions.

Therefore, the challenge is to balance 1) a reduction of wait time and its variance; 2) effectively utilize resources and minimize cost of POE operations, and 3) the sustainment of a security levels through Agent training, inspection and detection.
The intellectual merit of this proposal is based on using queueing theory and simulation on the border crossing process to implement methodologies that addresses port utilization and efficiency, which affects wait times, without increasing costs or affecting security procedures. An analytical model of a stochastic, non-stationary, and terminating queuing system is challenging because of the number of states in the system given the trucks at the POE.  A simulation model, validated through the analytical model, will serve to implement and test throughput improvement methodologies that do not affect cost or security procedures.  Improvements include the Dynamic Reallocation Methodology (DRM), lane availability policies, and the effect of influencing supply chain arrival data of commercial trucks. The second contribution addresses inspection (service) times under time-varying arrivals (demands). By developing secondary inspection policies, primary inspection time variance can be reduced. In the simulation model, a Markovian service time will be assumed first. However, prior work and field data suggest a general distribution that will be estimated using a Coxian k-phased approximation.  The third contribution is the development of a mobile app that will serve as a decision support application for the general public.  Current wait time sources are estimates at best.  An application that utilizes historical data can influence companies and people to select alternatives to congested border crossing points, and improve efficiencies.
The broader impact of this proposal applies to the international region that includes south Texas and northern Mexico.  Improvements will benefit border communities economically and the general population through increased security. Finally, by incorporating into current educational efforts, new engineers and the general public can be educated to make better decisions.

CONGRANT.TITLE: The Development of an Industrial Assessment Center for South Texas
CONGRANT.SPONORG: Department of Energy (DOE), Office of Energy Efficiency & Renewable Energy (EERE)
CONGRANT.ABSTRACT:
The four counties in deep south Texas known as the Rio Grande Valley are home to one of the fastest growing populations and one of the fastest growing manufacturing sectors in the state of Texas and world. The region is known as the Rio Grande Valley because it is located on the northern banks of the Rio Grande River which serves as the international boundary between the United States and Mexico. The Rio Grande Valley is also home to the second largest federally certified Hispanic Serving Institution (HSI) of higher education in the United States, the University of Texas Rio Grande Valley (UTRGV). Approximately 90% of the more than 25,000 UTRGV students are Hispanic.
The UTRGV College of Engineering and Computer Science (CECS) has been recognized for the quality of its academic programs and the numerous partnerships and collaborations that its faculty have established with more than 100 entities in its service area including manufacturers, local governments, economic development councils, two year institutions of higher education and not-for-profit organizations. The undergraduate degrees that the CECS awards in civil engineering, mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, manufacturing / industrial engineering and computer science engineering are all accredited by the Accreditation Board for Engineering and Technology (ABET).
There is a tremendous need for the creation of the South Texas Industrial Assessment Center (South Texas IAC). In spite of the Rio Grande Valley’s rapidly growing population and the growing manufacturing sector the closest Industrial Assessment Center (IAC) to deep south Texas is 350 miles away. The development of the South Texas IAC will provide industrial energy assessments to small and medium sized enterprises (SMEs) that previously did not have access to such no-cost energy assessments. Through the provision of these industrial energy assessments the South Texas IAC has the potential of assisting manufacturers to save millions of dollars each year in energy and water management costs.
The proposal to develop a South Texas Industrial Assessment Center (South Texas IAC) described herein is made possible because of a number of CECS engineering faculty who possess the requisite expertise and willingness to work with 20 UTRGV engineering students to carry out twenty industrial assessments per year. The faculty participating in the activities being proposed herein represent all of the departments in the CECS including electrical engineering, manufacturing and industrial engineering, civil engineering, and mechanical engineering. The diversity of faculty members’ areas of specialization and their various departmental affiliations in the CECS will provide students with an appreciation of the cross disciplinary nature of industrial energy assessments. The diversity of faculty will also ensure that engineering students throughout the CECS will become aware of the existence of the South Texas IAC and will have the opportunity to participate in the assessment activities as well as internships and research projects that come about as a result of the creation of the South Texas IAC.
As manufacturing enterprises in the Rio Grande Valley become aware of the tremendous financial benefits that accrue to them from the energy assessments offered through the South Texas IAC it is anticipated that small and large manufacturers alike will contribute to the financial viability of the South Texas IAC after grant funds expire.

CONGRANT.TITLE: Impact and Conversion Analysis of Used Tires from Environmental and Health Hazards into Raw Material Precursors in the Rio Grande Valley of Texas and Northern Tamaulipas.
CONGRANT.ABSTRACT: The existence of enormous numbers of used or scrap tires on both sides of the U.S. Mexico border is a major ecological and public health problem. They also provide excellent breeding grounds for mosquitoes and air-borne diseases such as, Zika, Chikungunya and West Nile virus. Unfortunately, most policy makers and members of the general public are unaware of the degree to which used tires are negatively affecting the quality of life on both sides of the border. The research project described herein proposes 1) to qualify and quantify the impact of both legally and illegally discarded used tires in the Rio Grande Valley and mapping data and import/export data analysis at the international ports of entry, and 2) to describe alternative conversion methods for used tires as raw materials. The results of this research will provide substantiated quantitative metrics that will 1) describe the precise magnitude of the problem in the region and 2) guide the investigation of suitable alternatives to provide cost effective and financially sustainable solutions.

INTELLCONT.TITLE: Estudio Termoquímico Asistido por Computadora de los Polifenoles presentes en la Fresa
INTELLCONT.PUBLISHER: Investigacion e Innovacion en ingenieria
INTELLCONT.ABSTRACT: Las fresas son un alimento importante en Latinoamérica debido a sus componentes químicos, puesto que son una considerable fuente de calorías y polifenoles. Estos elementos son útiles por su capacidad antioxidante y otras propiedades beneficiosas para la salud. Sin embargo, la presión y la temperatura pueden llegar a afectar la integridad molecular de estos componentes, por lo tanto, en el proceso de producción de diferentes productos basados en fresas, se requiere estudiar las propiedades termoquímicas de los diferentes polifenoles presentes en esta fruta. Para ello, se extrajeron datos de las principales familias de polifenoles, antocianinas, flavanoles, flavonoles, ácidos hidroxibenzoicos y ácidos hidroxicinámicos, y de cada familia se extrajeron los componentes con mayor presencia en la fresa. Para realizar el análisis termoquímico, se utilizaron las herramientas Aspen PropertiesV11® y Aspen PlusV11® , donde se simulo una mezcla de diferentes polifenoles en una base de agua que simula la composición de 100 g de fresa. En primer lugar, se observó el comportamiento termoquímico al aumentar la temperatura a presión constante las propiedades termoquímicas de los compontes puros. Luego, se realizó la segunda simulación donde la mezcla de los componentes en una fresa., como cianidina, pelargonidina, catequina (+)-, epicatequina (-), quercetina 3-O-glucuronida, ácido elágico, ácido cinámico y cafeoil glucosa fue evaluada a diferentes temperaturas, pero a presión constante. Se obtuvo que los componentes en su estado sólido tienen puntos de cambio de fase bastante altos en comparación con el agua, y sus puntos críticos, como el volumen crítico, la temperatura y la presión críticas, son el doble que los del agua (56,1234 cm³/mol, 374,228°C, 220,424 bar). Con lo anterior, se discuten las posibilidades industriales de estos elementos y su extracción por medios convencionales. Se validó el resultado con la presión de vapor obtenida para el ácido cinámico y se comparó con la del NIST, obteniendo un margen de error del 1%.
INTELLCONT.FULL_TEXT: hiram.moya/intellcont/Estudio Termoquímico Asistido de los Polifenoles en la Fresa-1.pdf

INTELLCONT.TITLE: Development of a Small-Business Data Management Pull System; A Case Study
INTELLCONT.PUBLISHER: Proceedings of the IISE Annual Conference & Expo 2023
INTELLCONT.EDITORS: K. Babski-Reeves, B. Eksioglu, D. Hampton
INTELLCONT.ABSTRACT: According to the U.S. Small Business Association, small businesses of five hundred employees or fewer make up 99.9% of all U.S. businesses [1]. However, 65% of new businesses fail within the first ten years of opening, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics. This case study will center around the used vehicle market, where small businesses that focus on buying and selling used cars have had issues with accurately tracking information due to the lack of a proper data-entry system. Despite the common use of a car, no thorough study has been done to develop or build an information tracking system at a small scale. Many companies lack a proper data management system to adequately manage the documentation of inventory. This lack of structure is costing companies money along with constant errors going undetected when inputting information. The tracker will be done in Excel, due to the widespread usage in small businesses. The manual data will be digitized and will keep track of inventory on hand. Using advanced functions and formulas in excel, the information tracker will be able to display necessary information for easy analysis. This system will use dynamic ranges for summations of expenses, dynamic tables, and dynamic XLOOKUP functions to allow the user to easily input data while minimizing the potential errors and creating an easy-to-read table of inventory. The expected result is to develop a simple information tracking system that allows the user to input all data necessary in small business applications.
INTELLCONT.FULL_TEXT: hiram.moya/intellcont/AMT - Dev Small-Business Data Mgmt Pull System-1.pdf

INTELLCONT.TITLE: Extending CONWIP Control to Multiple Servers with General Service
INTELLCONT.PUBLISHER: Proceedings of the IISE Annual Conference & Expo 2023
INTELLCONT.EDITORS: K. Babski-Reeves, B. Eksioglu, D. Hampton
INTELLCONT.ABSTRACT: Lean manufacturing techniques include the work-in-process (WIP) control mechanism of constant WIP (CONWIP). This paper generalizes the analytical tools of CONWIP to incorporate general service times, as represented by Coxian distributions, for multiple-identical servers per workstation. A two-phase Coxian is a weighted sum of two-exponential distributions and can match the mean and variance of a general distribution if the squared coefficient of variation (SCV) is greater than or equal to one-half. This analysis computes the mean values for cycle time, throughput rate, and WIP in each workstation and the system-as-a-whole. The solution methodology is based on the arrival theorem for closed queueing networks (CQN) and a solution method that iteratively increases the system’s WIP starting from one job until the maximum system’s WIP is reached. The marginal probability distribution for each workstation’s WIP under two-phase Coxian distributions with multiple identical servers is developed iteratively as system WIP increases. The expected remaining time for jobs in-service is developed using the moments’ equation for phase-type distributions. A MATLAB computer model was developed for a connected system of workstations with arbitrary random branching and a maximum of three servers per workstation. The results of this generalization agree with the known special case of multiple-exponential servers and the case of single servers with general service when represented by two-phase Coxian distributions. An example model of three workstations with two servers in each illustrates the methodology.
INTELLCONT.FULL_TEXT: hiram.moya/intellcont/Curry Bennett Moya - MultiServer CONWIP - IISE 2023 FINAL-1.pdf

INTELLCONT.TITLE: A Dedicated Lane Analysis for Supply Chain Resilience in the US-Mexico Border

INTELLCONT_AUTH.INSTITUTION: The University of Texas Rio Grande Valley
The University of Texas Rio Grande Valley
The University of Texas Rio Grande Valley

INTELLCONT.PUBLISHER: Proceedings of the IISE Annual Conference & Expo 2023
INTELLCONT.EDITORS: K. Babski-Reeves, B. Eksioglu, D. Hampton
INTELLCONT.ABSTRACT: Supply chain resilience is the capacity of a supply chain to quickly adapt to sudden disruptive changes so that the flow of goods is not affected. Due to the COVID-19 pandemic, it has become a major topic for transborder commerce. The US-Mexico border has dedicated lanes called Free and Secure Trade (FAST) for commercial vehicles. However, there is no prior record for a dedicated lane for a single company. Quietly in 2022, a lane was opened for Tesla’s suppliers at the border with the state of Nuevo León, Mexico. Of the limited number of studies on supply chain resilience that specifically address the transborder supply chain, only a few of these papers analyze the effects of FAST lanes and none analyze a dedicated lane for a company. This paper analyzes the impact of a dedicated lane by developing a Cost Comparison Model. Variables like delayed time, gas consumption due to wait time, and distance are analyzed to identify if there is a significant relationship with the response variable. The analysis shows that having a dedicated lane benefits the resilience of the supply chain. These results are used to compare them with other lanes and verify if there is a significant difference in cost. Future research can focus on developing a simulation to compare capacity percentage vs wait time of Tesla´s Lane.

INTELLCONT.TITLE: Assessing the Feasibility of a Biofilter in Medium-to-High Scale Industries
INTELLCONT.PUBLISHER: Proceedings of the 2020 IISE Annual Conference
INTELLCONT.ABSTRACT: The removal of volatile organic compounds, VOCs, from contaminated sources of air stream has become a major air pollution risk. Excessive amounts discharged to the atmosphere are highly risky to human health and to the environmental system. Demand for sustainable VOC control technologies has become crucial to ensure the reduction of emissions. Biological treatments of waste gas streams, such as biofiltration, have proven to be cost effective and environmentally friendly compared to conventional pollution control technologies. Yet, only a few studies on medium scale biofilters have been conducted before. In order to evaluate the optimal design of medium scale biofilters for treatment, the goal of this research is to simulate data for a given biofilter model, and to evaluate if it is economically and environmentally feasible to implement with a given set of conditions based on previous data. The model incorporates key parameters such as annual capital costs, investment costs, and annual operating costs. Results and observations are reported to show promise for developing a model that can routinely and reliable describe the effectiveness of a biofiltration system for medium scale industries.

INTELLCONT.TITLE: Evaluating Cross-Border Logistics and Compliance at the US Texas Border
INTELLCONT.PUBLISHER: Proceedings of the 2020 IISE Annual Conference
INTELLCONT.ABSTRACT: With more than eleven million trucks crossing the border annually, unexpected delays due to congestion, security risks, and staffing at the Ports of Entry (POE) are inevitable.  Many companies’ internal cross-border operations have several manual activities and manual data input that need to be verified at several points in the cross-border shipping and logistics process. This research maps out the current border-crossing process at the southern US border from two distinct business units with major import/export and logistics operations who have agreed to map out and participate in this research.  From the perspective of Customs and Border Protection (CBP), trade compliance is a major component for companies to participate in expedited and secure programs which can benefit an organizations performance and reputation.  In the United States these programs include Trusted Trader Programs, Trade Compliance and the Customs Trade Partnership Against Terrorism (C-TPAT).  Most of the cross-border logistics research focuses on external company activities to mitigate delays and reduce costs.  However, internal operations are the main source of compliance mistakes, and unnecessary costs.  The analysis identified three major areas: premium freight due to expediting, workload, and classification accuracy.  Results highlighted the need of more integrated Mexican-US logistical analysis, and compliance research.

INTELLCONT.TITLE: Reducing Wait Times at Laredo POE through CBP Officer Staffing
INTELLCONT.PUBLISHER: Proceedings of the 2020 IISE Annual Conference
INTELLCONT.ABSTRACT: The purpose of this study is to reduce delays at the Laredo ports of entry (POE) by adding United States Customs and Border Protection (CBP) Agency officers to its inspection stations. We use a stationary deterministic queuing system to model the traffic at the POE. The queue is shocked by adding CBP officers during the most congested hours of the inspection process. Wait times are quantified and then translated into border-related transportation costs. Finally, we analyzed the economic impact caused by these transport costs using a computable general equilibrium (CGE) model. We found that additional staffing decreased the cost of imports from Mexico into the U.S., decreasing the cost of production in the U.S. and making exports more competitive worldwide. Our study highlights how important trade policy is to cross-border supply chains.

INTELLCONT.TITLE: Blockchain Technology-enabled Supply Chain Systems and Supply Chain Performance:  A Resource-based View
INTELLCONT.PUBLISHER: Supply Chain Management: an International Journal
INTELLCONT.ABSTRACT: Purpose Using the resource-based theoretical view of the firm, this paper aims to explore how firms’ efforts to integrate blockchain technology (BCT) into their supply chain systems and activities enable certain supply chain capabilities and, consequently, improve their supply chain performance. Design/methodology/approach Using an abductive research approach, a qualitative content analysis was conducted on 126 cases of firms attempting to implement a blockchain technology-enabled supply chain system (BCTeSCS). These firms spanning across multiple industries were identified using the Nexis Uni database. Findings Findings reveal that present BCTeSCS efforts are more-oriented toward improving operational-level capabilities (information sharing and coordination capabilities) than strategic-level capabilities (integration and collaboration capabilities). These operational and strategic-level capabilities alongside BCTeSCS deliver several supply chains performance outcomes such as quality compliance and improvement, process improvement, flexibility, reduced cost and reduced process time. However, outcomes may vary by industry type based on their uncertainties. Research limitations/implications Given the nascent state of BCT, accessibility to primary data about ongoing BCTeSCS efforts is limited. The presented framework is based on 126 cases of secondary information. Within this constraint, the paper finds scope to future empirical research by proposing a resource-based framework of BCTeSCS and related propositions. Practical implications The results and discussion of this study serve as useful guidance for practitioners involved in BCTeSCS integrations. Social implications The paper creates a BCTeSCS scenario for stakeholders to assume its potential socio-economic and socio-environmental pressures. Originality/value This paper is one of the initial attempts to examine BCTeSCS efforts across multiple industries, and thus, promises a broad future research scope.

INTELLCONT.TITLE: Feasibility of Biofilters to Reduce Pollutant Emissions in Diesel Engines
INTELLCONT.PUBLISHER: Institute of Industrial and Systems Engineers
INTELLCONT.EDITORS: H.E. Romejin, A. Schafer. R. Thomas
INTELLCONT.ABSTRACT: Every year, heavy-duty diesel trucks (HDDV), such as commercial border trucks, idle for long periods of time waiting at the ports of entry, POE, of the United States, emitting gases such as, carbon monoxides (CO), Volatile Organic Compounds (VOCs), and oxides of nitrogen (NOx).These last two are not listed within the six critical pollutants by the Environmental Protection Agency, but they serve as precursors of ozone (O3), a major pollutant which has detrimental effects on human health and the environment. Among one of the emergent control technologies in existence is biofiltration. The biofiltration process allows the removal of contaminants present in the stream of air via biochemical oxidation of organic compounds by microorganisms. In this research, a biofilter for these vehicles is designed and adopted from existing biofilters to test the removal efficiency in diesel engines. The prototype of this design will be evaluated in the capture of emissions. This paper compares existing technologies and evaluates the feasibility of using a biofilter using basic principles such as, design, cost, process, and effectiveness. Other studies have indicated a greater than 90% efficiency, but design and costs for vehicle designed biofilters are still challenges to be pursued.

INTELLCONT.TITLE: Renewable Energies: Reducing Cost-by-Expansion of The RGV Electric Utility Companies.
INTELLCONT.PUBLISHER: Institute of Industrial and Systems Engineers
INTELLCONT.EDITORS: H.E. Romejin, A. Schafer. R. Thomas
INTELLCONT.ABSTRACT: According to Interstate Renewable Energy Council (IREC), Renewable energy systems are becoming prevalent and economically accessible for small-town municipalities in South Texas. Nowadays, the two most popular energy sources of the electrical utility companies, in the Rio Grande Valley (RGV), are coal and natural gas. When these companies think about an expansion in the electrical capacity, they face major economic issues escalated by the high costs of the current energy sources. The intention is to reduce cost by expansion of RGV electrical utility companies by knowing what fraction of their electrical current sources, a renewable energy system can provide while being economically advantageous unlike only a capacity based on coal and natural gas. This research will assess a renewable energy system as the third energy source for these electrical utility companies. The primary aim of this paper is to conduct the concept of levelized cost of energy (LCOE) to evaluate three renewable energy sources and determine which one is the most economically sustainable in RGV. To address the reliability and verify the results, a sensitivity analysis is conducted by executing a C++ code of the LCOE parameters of this research. The paper concludes that that depending on the technology employed; wind energy is the least expensive per unit (MWh).

INTELLCONT.TITLE: Risk Factor Simulation and Cost Estimation of Undiagnosed High Blood Pressure in Young Adults
INTELLCONT.PUBLISHER: IIE Transactions on Healthcare System Engineering
INTELLCONT.ABSTRACT: Current estimates for health costs are wide ranging to non-existent, yet they play a key role on the culture of preventive care, making early detection of asymptomatic conditions like high blood pressure (HBP) a challenge. To address this, a risk factor simulation model and annual expected cost function were developed to determine the annual expected cost of medical complications associated to misdiagnosis of HBP in young adults. The designed simulation estimated the likelihood of misdiagnosis for pre-hypertension, stage 1, and stage 2 hypertension in young males and females of different races/ethnicities. This estimate was included in an expected cost function to compute the individual economic impact. The models found that, at the national level, 60.53% of men and 59.72% of women ages 18 to 24 are at risk of misdiagnosis and could incur on individual annual expenses of up to $63,000 depending on the degree of their condition. The study also evaluated a case study of the South Texas population where the adjusted models estimated that about 62.64% of men and 61.72% of women are at risk of uncontrolled HBP due to lack of diagnosis and are expected to spend about the same as the nation to deal with complications of HBP.
INTELLCONT.FULL_TEXT: hiram.moya/intellcont/MTT Risk Factor Simulation and Cost Estimation Rev-1.pdf

INTELLCONT.TITLE: Analysis of Productivity Improvements Through  Energy Assessments in Texas
INTELLCONT.PUBLISHER: Institute of Industrial and Systems Engineers
INTELLCONT.EDITORS: K. Barker, D. Berry, and C. Rainwater
INTELLCONT.ABSTRACT: The manufacturing sector is a complex and ever evolving environment that is constantly incorporating the latest technology and efficiency principles in order to establish or maintain a competitive advantage.  Technology improvements are effective differentiators, but many companies need to look for cost savings opportunities, in order to remain profitable.  This research focuses on the analysis of productivity improvement through assessments done from the Industrial Assessment Centers (IAC) in Texas.  The Department of Energy (DOE) stablished the IAC program at different universities in order to provide free energy, productivity and sustainability assessments to small and mid-size companies.  Throughout the years, several IACs have served the manufacturing sector in Texas, but the majority of the assessments miscalculate the impact of energy savings through productivity projects or improvements, some of which are ignored or underestimated in the plant.  Initial research findings show that productivity improvements have an average low implementation rate of 42%. Through the use of the IAC database, this research investigates the number of productivity improvements and proposes a financial conversion methodology to assess productivity improvements, and addresses the low implementation rate.

INTELLCONT.TITLE: Minimization of Out-of-Pocket Expenses in the South Texas Region
INTELLCONT.PUBLISHER: Institute of Industrial and Systems Engineers
INTELLCONT.EDITORS: K. Barker, D. Berry, and C. Rainwater
INTELLCONT.ABSTRACT: According to the Center for Disease Control, the United States spends approximately $46 Billion every year on healthcare for high blood pressure (HBP) prevention, control, and treatment of associated complications. Out of the overall expenses for HBP, Out-of-Pocket expenses represent up to 21% of the entirety of the described costs. Current efforts to increase early diagnosis and treatment of HBP include building Specialized Medical Facilities (SMF) or buying Medical Mobile Units (MMU) to service different population areas. This research presents a comparative analysis of the possible out-of-pocket healthcare savings resulting from implementing SMF and MMU in the South Texas region. The implementation of SMF and MMU are evaluated through a three-objective function allocation algorithm and a linear optimization model respectively, which are able to determine the optimal amount and location of the facilities or mobile units to be implemented in order to minimize out-of-pocket costs considering healthcare expenses, hospitalization rates, and population size, among other cost-related factors. The models defined the optimal locations/deployment areas for the services and provided estimated savings between $83,000 to $12.3M depending on the previously determined improvement goals.

INTELLCONT.TITLE: Missing Energy Considerations in Industry Operational Improvements: Two Case Studies
INTELLCONT.PUBLISHER: Institute of Industrial and Systems Engineers
INTELLCONT.EDITORS: K. Barker, D. Berry, and C. Rainwater
INTELLCONT.ABSTRACT: According to the Department of Energy (DOE), optimizing the efficiency of manufacturing processes can result in significant energy and cost savings. Process efficiency can be achieved through the implementation of productivity improvements which often can translate into increased production capacity and larger profit margins. Although most companies try to generate productivity enhancements, there often exists a disconnection between such improvements and the associated energy expenses/savings resulting from them. Using the DOE’s Industrial Assessment Center database, and case studies of two companies in the manufacturing sector of South Texas, relevant missing energy considerations regarding Direct Productivity Enhancements are identified. Companies search for improvements in energy assessments, “energy treasure hunts” and consulting engagements, but miss properly quantifying the impact. The research question focuses on quantifying the impact of missed productivity enhancements. With tools such as lean engineering and decision support tools, the two case studies are used to compute the energy impact. A comparison was drawn between current energy recommendations savings and expected savings from applicable productivity enhancements. Future studies consist in a comparison between the expected savings from the productivity improvements and actual savings after applying the energy considerations, and, a review of limiting factors affecting the implementation of these improvements.

INTELLCONT.TITLE: Multiple Machine Feedforward Networks with Blocking
INTELLCONT.PUBLISHER: Institute of Industrial and Systems Engineers
INTELLCONT.EDITORS: K. Barker, D. Berry, and C. Rainwater
INTELLCONT.ABSTRACT: Almost all of the analytical decomposition approaches for queueing networks with limited WIP allow only single machine workstations.  This paper considers the development of a multiple-machines feed forward network analysis system for exponential servers and finite capacity workstations (Kanban control).  This approach can handle non-identical service rates for the different machines at the workstations. Multiple workstation systems quickly become too complex for a single steady-state model and decomposition into single workstation methods are utilized.  These results are connected via adjusted flows and increased delays and require an iterative scheme that cycles through the individual approximation systems in a manner such that the overall throughput result converges. The sequencing issue of blocked jobs causes the complexity of the merge configuration to increase significantly as the number of merging machine flows increases.  The aggregate state-space theorem is extended to the multiple machines/workstation case which allows a workstation sub-model with only one state for each level of the number of blocked jobs.  Then these aggregate probabilities yield the sequence-depend probabilities needed to develop the appropriate blocking probabilities for each inflow machine.  The approximation system performance measures agree quite well with simulation generated results.

INTELLCONT.TITLE: Wind Energy: An Assessment of Alternative Sources  for Texas Municipalities
INTELLCONT.PUBLISHER: Institute of Industrial and Systems Engineers
INTELLCONT.EDITORS: K. Barker, D. Berry, and C. Rainwater
INTELLCONT.ABSTRACT: According to the Global Wind Energy Council (GWEC), wind energy systems are becoming prevalent and economically accessible for small-town municipalities. With most municipalities depending on hydroelectric and fossils fuels, the question is what fraction of their electrical source, wind energy can provide while being economically advantageous. The Brownsville Public Utilities Board (BPUB) serves 730 miles in South Texas and is looking for alternative systems with inexpensive levelized cost. This research will assess wind system as an alternative due to its low cost of energy production. To determine how wind system has a long-lasting service, several elements of the wind system are evaluated. In addition, a case study is presented based on BPUB’S electrical production system and expected growth. From these values and using the LCEO calculator, the value of LCOE was found as $62.27 per MWH. Since the objective was to increase the power output by 25MW, the new plant size was 125MW. The effects of this change did not affect the value of LCOE significantly. Therefore, the change was seen to be feasible.

INTELLCONT.TITLE: A Deterministic Equivalent Problem to Study the Effects of Security Policies
INTELLCONT.TITLE_SECONDARY: Lecture Notes in Management and Industrial Engineering
INTELLCONT.PUBLISHER: Springer
INTELLCONT.EDITORS: Josefa Mula, Rafael Barbastefano, Manuel Díaz-Madroñero, Raul Poler
INTELLCONT.ABSTRACT: A Deterministic Equivalent Problem (DEP) is developed to understand the assignment of threats to secondary inspection at a U.S.-Mexican border port of entry, and how the overall assignment can affect security and the overall reward of further inspection. The United States and bordering countries benefit from the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA). But amongst the positive effects of NAFTA there is a looming drug threat that effects the overall flow of companies supply chains. In 2011, Customs and Border Protection (CBP) processed over 64,000 trucks, rail, and sea containers a day. During that 2011 Fiscal year CBP seized 5 million pounds of narcotics, including nearly 370,000 pounds at the ports of entry. The objective of the developed DEP is to incorporate real time data and to quantify how security officials assign threats to secondary inspection. This information can provide insight into staffing, resource allocation, and the disruption of industrial supply chains. This study will focus on the Pharr-Reynosa International Port of Entry. The expected outcome of the DEP will provide security officials insight into security policies and the associated cost associated with those strategies.
INTELLCONT.FULL_TEXT: hiram.moya/intellcont/Moya-Rueda LNCS New Global Perspectives on Industrial Engineering and Management final_v3-1.pdf

INTELLCONT.TITLE: Annual Expected Cost of High Blood Pressure in Young Adults
INTELLCONT.PUBLISHER: 2017 Industrial and Systems Engineering Conference
INTELLCONT.EDITORS: K. Coperich, E. Cudney, and H. Nembhard
INTELLCONT.ABSTRACT: Medical costs estimates are wide ranging or non-existent, yet they can influence preventive care, in particular asymptomatic conditions like high blood pressure (HBP).  To address this, a simulation model and expected cost function were developed to determine the annual expected cost of medical complications associated to misdiagnosis of HBP in young adults. According to the American Heart Association, adults 18 to 24 years old are 28% less likely of being diagnosed with HBP on regular medical visits compared to those 60 or older. The simulation estimated the average risk factor of false negatives in HBP diagnosis for young adults nationally. This estimate was included in the cost function to compute the individual economic impact. The models found that, at the national level, close to 40% of individuals is at risk of misdiagnosis and individual annual expenses could reach almost $92,000. This should motivate early-age blood pressure monitoring in order to preserve the physical and economic integrity of the young adult population. The study also evaluated a case study of the South Texas population where the adjusted models estimated that about 25% of young adults are at high risk of HBP and annual expected costs for misdiagnosed individuals was close to $100,000.

INTELLCONT.TITLE: Assessment Algorithm to Reduce Preventable Diabetes Hospitalizations in South Texas
INTELLCONT.PUBLISHER: 2017 Industrial and Systems Engineering Conference
INTELLCONT.EDITORS: K. Coperich, E. Cudney, and H. Nembhard
INTELLCONT.ABSTRACT: In the Rio Grande Valley (RGV) of South Texas, diabetes affects 1 in 4 individuals and according to the South Texas Diabetes & Obesity Institute, diabetes is the seventh leading cause of death in the United States.  2015 census data shows the South Texas population among the fastest growing with 1.5 million, in a geographical location that includes some of the poorest counties in the nation.  With the region’s poverty rate and prevalence of diabetes, the objective is to identify cost-savings based on reducing the rate of preventable hospitalizations due to diabetes long term complications.  These readmissions could be reduced with effective preventive care, saving Medicare/Medicaid which cover 70% of costs.  To achieve these goals, numerical cases are evaluated with the proposed Ranked Cost-Savings for Facilities Algorithm as an assessment model that considers costs and population impact.  The research question is what is the optimal number of facilities and in what counties they should be located, particularly for South Texas, which has a higher incidence of diabetes. Data is from the Texas Department of State Health Services Center for Health Statistics and other agencies. Results identify county facilities that can be justified depending on impact and cost.

INTELLCONT.TITLE: A modeling language generator for a discrete event simulation language in MATLAB
INTELLCONT.PUBLISHER: IEEE
INTELLCONT.ABSTRACT:
A discrete-event simulation language was implemented in MATLAB.  The modeling approach is similar to the process/command modeling paradigm utilized in GPSS as well as many languages that followed.  The language is implemented as a MATLAB Script File (m-file) and can be part of a larger analysis package such as being a sub-function of an optimization/simulation system.  Unlike other modeling efforts in MATLAB that do not use the standard modeling paradigm, the ease of model development with this approach makes it an effective modeling tool.  To take full advantage of the language requires some familiarity with MATLAB since all of its language power is directly available particularity the “for” and “if-else” structures and graphics support.  The full language is visible and as such can be enhanced and extended by the user. 
The basic simulation model is a function (m-file) that minimally is 200 lines of code.  However, the modeler generally writes only about 50 of these lines to develop simple models but must insert them in the proper locations and understand how the internal model is developed using the switch/cases statement to create the proper model operation.  To simplify this process, a model generator has been developed which parses a model text file and produces the required MATLAB master simulation function.  The model generator also reduces the magnitude of understanding of the implementation specifics of the MATLAB simulation language and makes proper model development easier.
